newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW - Amplats says S.Africa can't fill PGM gap.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Amplats says S.Africa can't fill PGM gap.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd said on Friday there was an acute shortage of platinum and palladium in the market which could only be relieved by the resumption of Russian supplies of the white metals.
Amplats managing director Barry Davison told Reuters he did not believe that South African primary producers of platinum and palladium had stocks to relieve the market.

"I don't believe that South African primary producers have stock of metal. I don't think the relief can come from here. The relief can only come from a resumption of Russian supplies and dishoarding of the metal," he added.
"There will be some relief clearly, once they (the Russians) start but whether that relief will be sufficient to cool down the market, I can't say -- I hope so," he added.
Spot platinum traded at seven-year highs in London after being fixed at $495.00 an ounce while its sister metal palladium traded at the highest level in 17 years after being fixed at $240.
"The situation is highly volatile, there is an extreme shortage of nearby metal. This is clearly caused by the fact that the Russians are not delivering," he said.
Davison said he would be surprised if prices stayed at present levels, stressing that the market could only expect relief when Russia resumes supply deliveries.
"We have heard market rumour that the Russians will resume deliveries during the course of June when their export licences are in place.
"The key question becomes at what rate will they deliver. We have said for some time now that we do believe that the Russian supply for calendar 1997 will be substantially reduced," Davison said.
